title: Amərətāt, spelled the way the sources wrote it

body:
# Amərətāt, spelled the way the sources wrote it
There is a version of this name the early internet had to settle for: *ameretat*. This is the file on how **Amərətāt** replaced it.

Amərətāt does not have a long narrative mythology of her own. She is one of the seven Holy Immortals who surround AhuraMazdā and help govern the created world. Her stories are embedded in cosmology, ritual, and eschatology rather than in heroic adventure. In Zoroastrian cosmogony, AhuraMazdā creates the plant world — the fourth of the seven creations (sky, water, earth, plants, cattle, man, and fire) — and assigns its guardianship to Amərətāt.  Angra Mainyu (Ahriman) responds by sending drought, locusts, and winter to wither the green world.

That is the figure this file is about — and the temple now standing at its restored name.
## At a Glance

- **Restored name:** Amərətāt
- **ASCII form:** ameretat
- **Meaning:** "Immortality"
- **Domain of influence:** Immortality, Plants
- **Pantheon:** Zoroastrian
- **Classification:** Tier 1
- **Original script:** 𐬀𐬨𐬆𐬭𐬆𐬙𐬁𐬙
- **Series:** The Restoration Files, No. 14 of 271
## The Name Before the Marks

Strip **Amərətāt** to *ameretat* and one piece of evidence vanishes:

- **a → ā** — Long vowel: the vowel length the ASCII form cannot show.

A reader who knows the marks hears the name correctly on the first try. A reader who never sees them never gets the chance.
## The Temple That Stands Now

The restored name is not a plaque; it is an address. The temple of **Amərətāt** lives at [/sites/ameretat/](/sites/ameretat/), with its mythology in the [lore halls](/sites/ameretat/lore/), its peer-reviewed record in the [Scholarly Edition](/sites/ameretat/scholars/), and its place in the pattern atlas on the [patterns floor](/sites/ameretat/patterns/).

The restoration preserves more than the ASCII form can say — stress, length, or a letter the Latin keyboard lost — which places it in Tier-1: mechanically verifiable, information-rich.

Every flagship temple is hand-built to the same standard: the original script displayed with its provenance, the pronunciation reconstructed phoneme by phoneme, the sources named — because a restoration you cannot audit is just a spelling with confidence.
## The Archetype at Work

A temple is also a reading of what this figure *means* — and meanings have addresses in the modern world. The [pattern atlas](/patterns/) maps **Amərətāt** to the industries its archetype genuinely resonates with, each match argued, weighted, and open to challenge:

- **Biotech, Longevity & Life Sciences** — Immortality personified in the Amesha Spenta of plants.
- **Agriculture, Food & Harvest** — Immortality dwelling in plants; the Zoroastrian patron of vegetation.
- **Environmental & Climate Services** — The sacred dimension of plant life; protecting the earth's green cover is a religious duty under her guardianship.

The mapping is conservative on purpose: only resonances that can be argued aloud. The rest of the atlas follows the same rule, industry by industry.
## In the Sacred Texts

The Zoroastrian tradition is not a vibe; it is a library. The [Sacred Texts collection](/texts/) holds [Avesta — Yasna & Yashts](/texts/avesta/) — the primary sources the temple's scholarship is built on, free to read, cross-linked back to the names they mention. The temple is the argument; the texts are the evidence.
